form.title: Job title
form.wantsHint: What they want to do. A profile pushed against their will leaves and resigns.
form.cvTextHint: Paste the existing CV. It is the raw material for tailoring to a mission — and the reference that prevents any experience being added that isn’t there.
form.kindHint: A candidate is an application file: the record is erased two years after the last contact.
form.engagementHint: How you staff them — independent of the nature.
form.managerHint: The person’s line manager, picked from the talent pool. Neither the client-side contact nor the account owner.
form.partnerHint: Without it, the record does not say who answers to the client.
form.publicProfileHint: The address the person gave you. Nothing is collected behind their back.
form.financeHint: Only visible with access to amounts.
form.costHint: Always entered, never computed. Without it, margin reads “not measured”.
form.mobilityHint: Leave blank until the person told you — the pool does not invent their answer.
form.siteFrequencyHint: How often they're expected on the client's premises — distinct from occasional travel.
form.internationalNo: Not open to an assignment abroad
form.mobilityRestrictionsHint: Plain text (driving licence, no overnight stays, childcare…) — no shared scale fits everyone.
form.processOtherInterviewsHint: Plain text: what we know of other processes, never guessed.
form.nonNegotiableConditionsHint: Plain text: what makes a mission unacceptable, never guessed.
form.refusedHint: Flagged in matching, never disqualifying: you are the one who talks to the consultant.
form.languagesHint: Comma-separated, level after a colon: fr:natif, en:b2. Without a level, we will ask.
form.clearancesHint: Comma-separated. A missing clearance blocks a submission.
form.financeOutOfScope: Rates are outside your scope. Loaded cost, purchase rate and minimum rate stay visible to whoever has that access.
form.consentBasisHint: Write it out: this wording is what commits your firm, not a ticked box.
form.consentBasisPlaceholder: Agreement given by email for an introduction to a client
form.consentRestrictionsHint: What the person EXCLUDED from their agreement — distinct from the legal basis above.
form.consentRestrictionsPlaceholder: No assignment at a direct competitor

consentState.none: Never collected. This is not “expired”: nobody has asked yet. The profile can still be submitted, and the absence is recorded on the submission.
consentState.expiring: Collected, but the agreement is close to lapsing. Ask again before it does.
consentState.expired: Collected, then expired. Until it is renewed, a submission will be refused.

form.stackTyping: One skill at a time. Each is recorded at level “unknown”, source “declared” — level and source are refined afterwards in the Skills tab of the profile.

duplicate.title: This person looks like someone you already have

form.yearsExperienceHint: Entered, never inferred — distinct from a skill's years of practice.
form.description: Fill in what you know. Apart from the name, nothing is required — everything can be completed later.

pool.title: To recontact
pool.intro: The people you have already met. Here are the ones worth recontacting.

explain.soon_available: Their assignment ends within 45 days. An assignment with no end date is not listed: we do not invent an availability.
explain.dormant: No contact for six months. Reaching out resets the clock — and extends how long you may keep their file.
explain.to_revalidate: Their record claims an availability no assignment confirms. That is not wrong data, it is unverified data: call them.
explain.never_submitted: Reviewed, ready, and never put in front of anyone. This is the pool you built without using it.
explain.recoverable_rejects: Rejected for a reason that says nothing about them: price, timing, cancelled need. Worth pitching elsewhere.
explain.rare_profiles: Fewer than three people carry their skill. Losing them costs a capability, not a profile.
explain.archived: Out of the active pool, data kept. A need can bring them back.

compatible.title: Structurally compatible environments
compatible.subtitle: What market observations have recorded, in the past, around this profile — a trace, never a current event.

buckets.verifiedUnmeasuredReason: No verification has been requested on this list from this workspace. "Not measured" is not "none".

compatible.fitNoGrade: No grading, and no score: calling it “strong” or “moderate” would require comparing each environment to peer companies of similar size and sector, which isn’t something we can do yet.
compatible.zoneUnknown: No area observed for this company in the corpus.
compatible.restrictionReason: A warning, never an exclusion: the company stays in this table and the verdict doesn’t move because of it — it’s the salesperson who decides.
compatible.currentSignalReason: No current signal — no dated observation is readable for this company: either none of your accounts points to it, or too few workspaces have observed it for a date to be stated without pointing to who saw it. This column never comes from market observations, which only carry a trace of the past.
compatible.signalSharedGrain: to the month — an exact date would point to who observed it
compatible.followedReason: No shared identifier (SIREN) between market observations and your accounts makes this reliably knowable.

dismissed.hideAria: Hide {{name}} — personal, no effect on other workspace members

verification.optional: Verification stays optional: this whole table reads and works without ever running one. An unverified row SAYS so, it is never locked.

stateReason.to_verify: No verification has been run on this company from this workspace. That is not a flaw in the row: verification is optional.
stateReason.unknown: The last verification could not measure anything (it timed out) — that is not a failure, and nothing is retried on its own.
stateReason.stale: The verification has aged: the fact is unknown again. The previous row is kept, it was not deleted.

import.title: Import without re-keying
import.description: One window: each import keeps its own report, nothing is merged without your review.

options.csv: Pool profiles — a CSV file (under 1 MB): name, job title, skills, city, email.
options.zip: A CV archive: a reliable profile updates itself, an ambiguity is set aside for review.
options.mail: An attachment from a thread your connected mailbox can already read.
options.single: One CV or skills file (PDF, DOCX): a single profile, created then reviewed by you.
options.availability: Availability (.csv, .xlsx) — updates existing profiles, never creates one.

import.cvBody: PDF or Word, several files, a folder, a ZIP archive or an email attachment. Each CV read creates or completes a qualified profile; the original is kept with its preview.
import.csvPreview: The CSV is previewed before anything is added. An identity matching at 0.99 or more is merged on its own, and reversibly; below that, it is proposed to you.

options.ats: The active pool in ATS format, downloaded right away (with a row cap).
options.bulk: The whole pool as a background job, no cap. Keep this window open until the download.

erase.body: This is GDPR erasure (Article 17): each selected profile — skills, experience, CV, prepared messages, submissions, finished assignments and what {{copilot}} remembered about the person — is deleted for good, with no way back. Archiving, by contrast, can be undone.
erase.trace: {{brand}} keeps only a trace with no personal data — who erased, when, and a non-reversible fingerprint — so the person is not recreated by an import or a CV upload. Payments already issued stay (accounting records), with no link to the person.
erase.skippedNote: A profile still assigned to an ongoing mission is left in place, with its reason stated: end or remove the assignment first.
erase.failed: The deletion could not be done.

reasons.not_found: A profile was already gone or outside your workspace.
reasons.forbidden: Only a workspace administrator or the profile’s owner can delete it.
reasons.blocked: An ongoing assignment holds it: end it first.

summary.declaredWins: Declared availability stays distinct from the mission schedule — and takes precedence when it exists.
